items.stem: A business can tolerate losing at most 15 minutes of data. Which objective does this define?

options.rationale: Correct: RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss, measured as a point in time.
RTO is how long recovery may take, not how much data may be lost.
MTBF measures reliability, not acceptable data loss.
The backup window is when backups run, not the loss tolerance.

items.explanation: Correct: RPO is the maximum acceptable data loss, measured as a point in time.

items.stem: Which two properties make a backup copy resilient against ransomware that tries to delete or encrypt backups? (Select TWO)

options.text: Immutability so the copy cannot be modified or deleted for a set period
options.rationale: Correct: immutability blocks tampering and deletion.

options.text: An air-gapped or offline copy not reachable from the production network
options.rationale: Correct: an unreachable copy cannot be encrypted by network-borne ransomware.

options.text: Storing the backup on the same server it protects
options.rationale: Co-locating the backup exposes it to the same compromise.

options.text: Granting all users write access to the backup store
options.rationale: Broad write access makes deletion or encryption easier.

items.explanation: Correct: immutability blocks tampering and deletion.; Correct: an unreachable copy cannot be encrypted by network-borne ransomware.

items.stem: Why is a successful backup job not sufficient proof that you can recover?

options.text: Only a tested restore confirms the data is complete and usable within the RTO
options.rationale: Correct: backups can succeed yet be unrestorable; restore testing proves recoverability.

options.text: Backup jobs always silently corrupt data
options.rationale: Jobs do not always corrupt data; the point is recovery must be tested.

options.text: Restores are illegal without a court order
options.rationale: Restores are a normal operation, not a legal event.

options.text: A backup job deletes the original data
options.rationale: Backups copy data; they do not delete the source.

items.explanation: Correct: backups can succeed yet be unrestorable; restore testing proves recoverability.
